clue.text: Steps up the retreat

explanation.surface: Someone climbs stairs up to a hideaway, the retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase run is a flight of steps, and fleeing in retreat is taking flight.

clue.text: Learned for the most part on river printed matter

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next, so the first comes before
most of the word, not all of it, is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: learned, in the sense of well-read, means literate
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A scholarly person writes about a river for a printed publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims the last E from LITERATE, leaving LITERAT; 'on' puts it above URE, the Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: Writings collectively, books and the like, are literature, a broad word for published written works.

clue.text: Stare at extreme characters for example turning out

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the turned letters wrap around the other piece
turning round means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: for example is abbreviated e.g.
A and Z are the characters at the two extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone looks hard at letters at the ends of the alphabet, perhaps in a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes GE of EG, and 'out' sets G and E outside AZ.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaze is to look long and steadily, a synonym for staring.

clue.text: Breathtaking

parts.note: read literally, taking someone's breath away by squeezing the windpipe rather than by being stunning

explanation.definitionFit: Strangling literally takes the breath from a victim, the grim literal sense of a word normally meaning amazing.

clue.text: Purely theoretical, it is over our heads on sunny days

definitions.text: it is over our heads on sunny days

explanation.surface: Abstract thinking is described as something far above us on a fine day.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-sky thinking is speculative and visionary, and a cloudless day shows a blue sky overhead.

clue.text: Droop with immediate loss thus initially

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the four preceding words

explanation.surface: A plant sags at once, losing vigour straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that wilt sag and go limp, which is drooping.

clue.text: Union restriction less often seen nowadays on a Sunday

definitions.text: less often seen nowadays on a Sunday

explanation.surface: Old trade-union rules and Sunday shopping laws have both faded in modern Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: A closed shop is a workplace where only union members may be employed, now largely outlawed in the UK; since Sunday trading was legalised in 1994, a shop shut on Sundays is rarer too.
explanation.definitionFit: A workplace limiting hiring to union members was a closed shop, and a store not trading on Sunday is a closed shop.

clue.text: Fuss over northern Ireland's handsome youth

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed over, above, the rest

parts.note: a fuss is an ado, as in much ado about nothing
I is an abbreviation for Ireland, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A bother arises about a good-looking young man from Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Adonis was a beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so the name stands for any handsome young man.

clue.text: Is in Palestine or off the coast of Northumberland

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the name for Palestine

parts.note: Palestine is known to Christians, Jews and Muslims as the Holy Land
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of geography: is a place in the Middle East, or off the English coast?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' reads as a verb but is fodder. Northumberland is England's most northerly county, and Lindisfarne lies off its coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lindisfarne, the tidal island site of an early monastery, is commonly called Holy Island and sits just off the Northumbrian shore.

clue.text: Charitable event noble arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman organises a fundraising event for a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges the letters of EVENT and NOBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A benevolent person is kindly and generous, giving to those in need, which is what charitable means.

clue.text: Bird, one ousted by young lover

indicators.note: ousted means thrown out, so the letter for one is removed from the word

parts.note: a swain is a poetic word for a young suitor or lover
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A suitor pushes aside a rival, one bird among many.
explanation.definitionFit: The swan is a large, long-necked water bird.

clue.text: The shopping area in London?

parts.note: a covered shopping precinct shares its name with the grand processional avenue from Trafalgar Square to Buckingham Palace

explanation.walkthrough: The Mall is a London avenue, not a place for shopping, so the question mark flags the play on a shopping mall.
explanation.definitionFit: A precinct full of stores is a mall, and The Mall is the royal road in central London leading to Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: Having gone first, Ernest had stockings inside leather shorts

parts.note: to have gone first is to have led

indicators.note: inside places the word for stockings within the short name

parts.note: Ern is a familiar short form of the name Ernest
hose is an old word for stockings

explanation.surface: Ernest led the way in his stockings and leather trousers, a picture of Bavarian costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had ... inside' is the container signal; Ern is the familiar short form of Ernest, as in the comic Eric Morecambe's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lederhosen are traditional Alpine knee-length breeches made of hide, worn in Bavaria and Austria.

clue.text: Be instructed to become ordained

explanation.surface: Someone accepts commands and joins the priesthood.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept commands is to follow instructions, and entering holy orders means becoming a priest.

clue.text: Do better than someone else emerging from troupe

definitions.text: Do better than someone else emerging from troupe

parts.words: Do better than someone else emerging from troupe
parts.note: a performer who steps out from the rest of a company to shine surpasses the others, a description of excelling rivals

explanation.definitionFit: To surpass a rival in achievement is to beat them, the standard sense of excelling over others.

clue.text: Instigator troubled grenadier travelling round lake

indicators.note: travelling round means the scrambled letters go around the letter for lake
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the word are mixed up

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: An anxious soldier walks around a lake, inciting trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges GRENADIER into RINGEADER, and 'travelling round' puts it around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader is the person who leads others into mischief or rebellion, so an instigator.

clue.text: In an advantageous position with money inside

parts.note: quids is British slang for pounds, so money
inside means in

explanation.surface: Someone sitting pretty with cash stashed away.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIDS IN is British slang for being in profit; a quid is a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for being in profit or comfortably ahead, the idiom means well placed.

clue.text: Practising the art of eating out

definitions.text: Practising the art of eating out

parts.words: Practising the art of eating out
parts.note: reads like dining in restaurants, but describes an art in which acid corrodes lines into a metal plate

explanation.definitionFit: The printmaking craft uses acid to bite designs into metal, an artist's technique of engraving with chemicals.

clue.text: Tool piercing board is subject to duty

indicators.note: piercing means going through, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging
ax is the American spelling of axe, a chopping tool

explanation.surface: A carpenter's tool goes through a plank, and the job is taxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piercing' signals the container; the tool uses its American spelling, without the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or income that attract a levy are taxable, liable to a duty.

clue.text: Step not made by one going forwards

definitions.text: Step not made by one going forwards

parts.words: Step not made by one going forwards
parts.note: a backward move, the opposite of progress, phrased as a literal footstep

explanation.definitionFit: A backward move is the kind of setback described by this adjective, going in reverse.

clue.text: I creep over to produce formula

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the letters of the words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks across a room to create a method.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook's set of instructions for a dish is a formula for making it.

clue.text: Whitish stake

explanation.surface: A fence post that has been bleached.
explanation.definitionFit: A wan, colourless shade is pale, and a pointed wooden post driven into the ground is a pale, as in a fence.

clue.text: 51 in company of muse

indicators.note: in tells us the numeral goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A number is in the company of an artist's inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals for numbers are a crossword staple; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Clio is the Greek Muse of history, one of nine daughters of Zeus.

clue.text: Motorists' preserve?

parts.note: reads as if a fruit conserve for drivers, but describes a congestion of cars

explanation.definitionFit: A queue of stationary cars on a road is a congestion, and a jam is also a fruit preserve.

clue.text: Sound horn up and down

indicators.note: the word reads the same going up the grid as down, so it is the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A driver honks as the car goes up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up and down' says the letters read the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To toot is to give a short blast on a horn or whistle.

clue.text: Firm in the money

parts.note: CO, short for company, means a firm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business is flush with cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin is a metal piece of currency, so money.

clue.text: One of the field parking has splendid hat

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
ace means excellent or splendid
a bowler is a hard, round-crowned felt hat

explanation.surface: A spectator at a field event parks while wearing a fine hat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielding side is the field; a pace bowler is a fast bowler, and a bowler is also a round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast bowler in cricket is one of the fielding team, which is collectively called the field.

clue.text: Fellow drawing back to get sacred text

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: back means the word for drawing is read in reverse

parts.note: drawing is a form of art

explanation.surface: A man withdraws in order to obtain a holy scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes TRA; 'Fellow' and 'drawing back' sit side by side in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sacred word or verse chanted in Hindu and Buddhist practice, so a holy text.
